citation: Huang Jiayu, Zhao Yeqian, Jiang Chuanhe, et al. Diagnostic efficiency of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for suspected infection in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients: a multicenter retrospective study. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, 2023.

population.population_description: Febrile allo-HSCT recipients with suspected infection; 271 paired mNGS/CMT samples, 258 samples analyzed after excluding 13 paired samples from the same febrile event

neutropenic_status: Samples grouped by neutropenic status at sampling: cohort A neutropenia n=92 samples, cohort B non-neutropenia n=179 samples

specimens.type: other (lung biopsy 2, urine 1, mucosal secretions 2, pleural effusion 2)

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS; positivity: bacteria/fungi SMRN >=3 at species level + genus relative abundance >30%; viruses SMRN >=3; parasites SMRN >=100

reference_standard: Independent clinical committee (two hematologists, one pulmonologist, one radiologist) adjudicated final diagnosis (clinically significant infection / infection without clinical significance / immune events / mixed) from symptoms, radiology, CMT and treatment response

comparator_2x2.against: conventional microbiological tests (CMT: smear, culture, G test, GM test, PCR for CMV/EBV etc.) - mNGS result vs CMT positivity, all 258 samples

diagnostic_yield.basis: mNGS positive detection rate 76.4% vs CMT 43.8% (P<0.001). Versus clinical reference standard (clinically significant infection): mNGS sensitivity 81.1%, specificity 56.5%, PPV 80.7%, NPV 57.4% (all 258 samples); blood specimen mNGS sensitivity 77.4%, specificity 52.6%; combination protocol sensitivity 88.3%

additional_yield_vs_conventional: Of 30 CMT-negative infected cases in cohort A, mNGS matched final causative pathogens in 20 (10 bacterial, 2 fungal, 5 viral, 3 polymicrobial); in cohort B mNGS verified 7 bacterial, 3 fungal, 26 viral, 5 polymicrobial infections in CMT-negative infected patients; P. jirovecii detected only by mNGS; 13/14 Aspergillus cases detected via mNGS vs 1 via CMT
therapy_change: Treatment success rate of targeted anti-infection strategy 85% (34/40) when based on mNGS vs 56.5% (26/46) with empirical therapy (P=0.004) in the 86 reviewed patients

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Paired mNGS/CMT from same specimens; mNGS results part of adjudication material (incorporation risk); multiple samples per patient (258 samples/153 patients, non-independent)

quadas2_notes: 2x2 extracted from Table 3 (mNGS vs CMT, total specimens n=258: CMT+/mNGS+ 90, CMT+/mNGS- 23, CMT-/mNGS+ 94, CMT-/mNGS- 51). Note this 2x2 is against CMT positivity, not the clinical reference standard; against clinical diagnosis only sensitivity/specificity are given without raw counts.

evidence_quotes.quote: We performed mNGS and CMT on samples obtained from 153 patients with suspected infection during allo-HSCT. ... we included 271 samples with parallel results for mNGS and CMT from 153 participants.

We retrospectively analyzed the medical records of patients who received allo-HSCT at Ruijin Hospital, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University, and Liquan Hospital, GoBroad Medical Institute of Hematology (Shanghai Center) from April 2021 to January 2023.
The positive detection rate of mNGS was 76.4%, significantly higher than 43.8% of CMT (P<0.001).
our results showed that the sensitivity of mNGS (81.1%) was significantly higher than that of CMT (53.6%) for clinical infection requiring intervention.
We divided these samples into two cohorts based on neutropenic status at the time of sampling: cohort A (neutropenia [n=92]) and cohort B (non-neutropenia [n=179])
The most frequent mNGS sampling specimen was peripheral blood (78.2%), followed by BALF (10.7%), CSF (8.5%), and others (2.6%).
The overall treatment success rate (TSR) was 85% (34/40) for patients treated based on the mNGS results, and 56.5% for those receiving empirical therapy (26/46, P=0.004
Immune events were diagnosed in 57.4% (35/61) of the febrile events with negative mNGS results, and 33.5% (48/143) with negative CMT results (P=0.002).
